newsitem.title: USA: Broadcasters want 'must-carry' rule for Sky - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Broadcasters want 'must-carry' rule for Sky - WSJ.

text.p: U.S. television broadcasters will argue in a government filing that News Corp's proposed Sky satellite-television venture should have to carry the on-air signals of all local stations, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.

Daily Variety said Time Warner vice-chairman Ted Turner was personally and energetically urging networks to reject News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch's ASkyB. Variety cited industry lobbyists involved in talks between the networks and News Corp.

According to the Journal, broadcasters say in a written testimony expected to be filed with the U.S. Copyright Office: "No rational distinction can be fashioned for exempting satellite carriers from a 'must-carry' requirement."
Broadcasters are comprised of the 650 affiliate stations of the three biggest networks, the newspaper said.
They also argue satellite services like Sky should be subject to a federal law which bans owning television and cable stations in the same market, the paper said.
Murdoch has said he could live with a limited 'must-carry' rule, the newspaper said. EchoStar Communications Corp is also involved in the Sky venture.
